title: From Chatbots to Confidants: A Cross-Cultural Study of LLM Adoption for Emotional Support

bias_targets.methodology: Large-scale user survey across seven countries (USA, UK, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Netherlands) and Cumulative Link Mixed Model analysis comparing LLM adoption rates, trust, and perceived benefits to identify geographic and cultural divides (e.g., Anglosphere vs. Continental Europe).

Analyzing user survey responses using mixed models to evaluate how subjective socioeconomic status (measured via the MacArthur Scale) correlates with disparities in trust, perceived benefits, and usage intentions of LLMs for emotional support.
Comparing self-reported survey data across distinct age demographics to evaluate age-related gaps in LLM adoption, positive perceptions, and psychological barriers.
Evaluating differences in system perception, trust, and usage intention between religious believers and non-believers using demographic survey data and mixed-model analysis.
